Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

specifically adverb

expressly, by name

also expressly, by name, in so many words, explicitly

classical

Cic. Att. 11.6.2: nōn nōminātim sed generātim (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Off. 3.65: nisi nōminātim dictum esset (Lewis & Short)

nōminātim

adverb · Wiktionary

specifically, by name, expressly

Literally “by name”: naming persons or things one by one, as opposed to generātim, “in general”. In Plautus also “one by one, in detail” (Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • disertē — expressly, in so many words

    adverb · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 4.1.6 (Lewis & Short); Liv. 21.19 (Lewis & Short) · Wiktionary

    Of what is stated outright, “clearly, distinctly”. From disertus, eloquent, and so it also means “eloquently” (Lewis & Short).

  • praecipuē — specifically, in particular, above all

    adverb · also used · classical · Sen. Ep. 7.1: quid tibi vītandum praecipuē exīstimēs quaeris? · Wiktionary

    For “specifically” in the sense “in particular”; see particular and especially.

Examples

  • nōn nōminātim sed generātim

    not specifically, but in generalCic. Att. 11.6.2 (Lewis & Short)

  • quicquid esset in praediō vitiī, id statuērunt, sī vēnditor scīret, nisi nōminātim dictum esset, praestārī oportēre

    they ruled that any defect in a property that the seller knew of must be made good, unless it had been specifically declaredCic. Off. 3.65 (Lewis & Short)

See also particular, especially.
